b: Essays from designers in the middle of the AI storm.

Most conversations about AI in design are about how. How other teams are prototyping with it, how AI is making them more productive, what it’s doing to user research, and what’s happening to the much-chased “design process.” Humankind goes the other way, and looks at what’s shifting inside the people doing the work.

This is an experimental series written by designers who are living through this like everyone else, struggling, learning, and unlearning along the way. In a way, it’s also an evolution of the State of UX we used to publish here on the UX Collective at the end of every year. But now, looking inward.
We don’t have answers. What we have is a growing list of questions, and they’re probably the best summary of what the series is about:
Who are we becoming while the tools make us faster and more sure of ourselves?
What do we want to keep doing slowly, even when we don’t have to?
What do we owe each other, and the things we make?
What do we lose when nothing is hard anymore, and would we notice?
Where do we still go to not know?
We’re still figuring most of this out.
What working with AI is doing to us was originally published in UX Collective on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.
